scope: Current donor source forensics plus current Claude Code external-primary capability crosscheck for native child-agent identity/lifecycle instrumentation. This packet does not claim the installed host version exposes or fires the documented ABI; host/runtime proof remains required.

atoms.what_it_does: handoff() creates an entityos_arbeitspaket row, builds a deterministic transition capsule from UnifiedDB-derived state, records advisory file leases/collision hints and returns the capsule. Its own docstring explicitly states that stern delegates nothing itself.
atoms.why_it_exists: Make delegated work durable and evidence-bearing while keeping coordinator/worker communication compact.
dependencies: external coordinator/native spawn path not implemented by handoff()
atoms.failure_mode: A durable workpackage can exist without an exact spawned child identity because handoff() has no spawn operation or child actor binding.
atoms.concurrency_implication: File leases are advisory collision hints rather than hard ownership locks, so child attribution/isolation must be established elsewhere.
atoms.latency_or_cost_implication: Keeping implementation detail in child contexts can reduce coordinator context growth, but this benefit is not measured by donor source alone.
known_counterevidence: The actual current native child spawn mechanism is not in this function and current host ~/CLAUDE.md/runtime ABI has not been observed in this packet.
open_questions: Which exact current host/native mechanism consumes this capsule and creates the child?
How is package_id bound to native agent_id/task_id at spawn time?

atoms.what_it_does: The pinned donor plugin registers exactly seven event classes through stern.py: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd and PreCompact. It does not register dedicated SubagentStart, SubagentStop or Task lifecycle hooks.
atoms.why_it_exists: Single-dispatcher hook consolidation for the current donor plugin.
inputs: seven configured Claude hook event classes
atoms.failure_mode: Dedicated native child lifecycle identity is not captured by this plugin configuration. Generic tool hooks could still receive child identity from a capable runtime, but current stern.py contains no agent_id or tool_use_id handling, so that identity is not durably bound by the inspected donor path.
atoms.concurrency_implication: Parallel child events can collapse toward parent/session-level bookkeeping unless actor/task/invocation identity is explicitly captured.
runtime_entrypoints: configured plugin hook scheduler if this exact hooks.json is loaded
known_counterevidence: Current host/global settings may register additional hooks outside the versioned donor plugin; this packet has not observed that host configuration.
open_questions: Does the installed host add SubagentStart/SubagentStop/Task hooks elsewhere?
Does the installed runtime place agent_id/agent_type in generic PreToolUse/PostToolUse payloads on this host?

atoms.what_it_does: Current official Claude Code documentation describes a native Agent/subagent path with unique agent_id in SubagentStart/SubagentStop, agent_id/agent_type on tool hook inputs inside subagents, resumable child instances by agent ID, nested subagents with a configurable depth limit, and optional worktree isolation.
atoms.why_it_exists: Provide native child execution/lifecycle capabilities that Frankenstein may be able to govern instead of reimplementing a parallel agent runtime.
reads: Claude Code configuration and subagent definitions
writes: runtime-managed child transcript/state; exact host behavior depends on installed build/config
atoms.failure_mode: Treating current documentation as proof of the user's installed runtime would silently upgrade a capability description into runtime evidence.
atoms.concurrency_implication: Native agent_id plus optional worktree isolation are promising primitives for exact actor/work ownership, but must be observed on the installed runtime before Triggerword-4 credit.
atoms.privacy_implication: Subagent context/config inheritance must be measured on host before deciding what owner/project instructions are propagated.
atoms.latency_or_cost_implication: Native delegation has spawn/context overhead; the owner-original therefore requires DIRECT_SMALL versus DELEGATE_BUILD efficiency classification.
runtime_entrypoints: documented Agent/subagent facility; installed reachability unverified
tests_or_receipts: official Claude Code documentation snapshot reviewed 2026-08-28
known_counterevidence: Installed version/build and managed settings are unobserved; documented current behavior may not match the target host.
open_questions: What exact Claude Code version/build is installed?
Which documented lifecycle fields fire on that build?
Does worktree isolation behave as documented in the target repository/runtime?

hypotheses: Frankenstein 2.0 can obtain most of the R2 child-harness substrate by binding entityos_arbeitspaket successors to the installed Claude native agent_id/task/lifecycle ABI rather than building a duplicate spawn runtime.
The largest current donor gap is not absence of delegated-work state but absence of exact actor/task/invocation binding between durable workpackages and the native child lifecycle.
counterhypotheses: The installed Claude Code build or managed settings may not expose the current documented native lifecycle ABI, forcing a bounded headless or custom wrapper path.
The actual current host may already add SubagentStart/SubagentStop or agent_id capture outside the versioned donor plugin, making the apparent donor identity gap only a repository-visibility gap.
Native agent_id alone may be insufficient for safe parallelism if filesystem/worktree/edit/effect ownership remains shared or mutable.
contradictions: The project architecture and owner policy expect spawned build agents, while the pinned donor handoff() explicitly does not spawn and the versioned plugin does not register dedicated child lifecycle hooks; preserve this as an unresolved integration boundary rather than assuming an invisible mechanism.
Current official docs expose identity/lifecycle primitives that could close the gap, but installed-runtime evidence is absent and must not be inferred from documentation.
Durable file leases exist but are advisory only, while Triggerword-4 requires stronger parallel child attribution/ownership before whole-system credit.
critical_unknowns: Exact current host ~/CLAUDE.md relevant delegation span/hash and whether it matches the owner-original policy.
Exact installed Claude Code version/build and enabled native Agent/subagent facilities.
Actual current spawn call path that consumes the handoff capsule.
Observed SubagentStart/SubagentStop/Task/tool hook payloads and stable agent_id/task_id/tool_use_id on target host.
Whether child and parent share the same worktree by default on target runtime and whether isolation: worktree is available/enabled.
How package_id is preserved across resume/replacement and parent restart.
Measured coordinator-context growth difference between DIRECT_SMALL/central execution and delegated multi-step execution.
